subject: ist-f
title: IST.F.------SOC.RT.
description: Diagram in AF(D)-38 (Affinity Dynamics, Level One) accompanying Braxton's claim that 'in the final analysis, all of these concepts do translate on the physical universe level — which is to say, our actual lives are related to what has happened from the distortion of true information.' (C)IST-F (the concept of interior-source functionalism) is crossed with SOC-RT (social reality): the question is what interior-source-functionalism produces when crossed with social-reality — when distortion has made interior-source-functionalism an isolated, controlled phenomenon. SOC-RT sits at the upper-center with CULT-INFO-DY (culture-information dynamics) on the upper-right. POST (postulation) anchors the upper-right output. INTR (interior) sits centrally between subject and partner. AFL (affinity alignment) hangs on the right of the central axis. POL-DYM (political dynamics) anchors the right output. INFO-ALGN (information alignment) feeds upward from below into the central axis. IF-ST-DY (information-style dynamics) sits below the crossing line. Structural argument: interior-source-functionalism crossed with social-reality is mediated by interior as central hub — Braxton's structural commitment that real social-reality emerges only when interior is live. The lower upstreams (information-alignment, information-style-dynamics) expose that without alignment of the *style* of information (which Braxton's chapter has shown to be western-skewed), the crossing produces culture-information-dynamics that flows into postulation and political-dynamics — i.e., into operational politics — rather than into affinity-alignment. The diagram is the structural case that *isolated* functionalism (the prose context) is the consequence of interior failing to operate as the hub.
